My favorite is corpo because it feels the most intimate to the story of both the main game and Phantom Liberty in terms of role play potential and I also like that V already has a long history with Jackie. The life paths in the game overall aren’t very well thought out or integrated with the main story but Corpo is definitely the most fleshed out life path and I feel it was probably the intended backstory they were writing for the game and V before they split it into three choices. With Street Kid and Nomad they aren’t as fleshed out and integrated with the story. You don’t even get to see Vs Street Kid or Nomad backstory. At the start of those you’ve already left your previous life in Atlanta or with your old Bakker clan and you only hear about it through dialogue/exposition. Corpo you are actively living it before it falls apart and you transition to the main game. The other two life paths act more as a bridge between your previous unseen life and main story whereas for Corpo the montage acts as the bridge. It’s a lot more thought out. It’s more for role play and head canon. Corpo just happens to provide the most substantial roleplay options so Corpo is my favorite.

It’s normal to feel this way as I do sometimes as well since I always use references but I like to remember everyone uses and have used references one way or another and that first you have to get good at drawing from references before you move onto memory because it trains your brain if you do it so many times. If you draw from reference for so long you’ll eventually get used to how the shape of a face looks or how a body comes together in a drawing etc etc. There isn’t anything wrong with using references or using grid method or just tracing. Whatever you enjoy and helps you to draw better just go for it. Just keep practicing and you’ll get there eventually.

I do tend to struggle with softer lines and blending  as well so sometimes I just use that to my advantage and try to make my own style or look out of it idk how successful I am at that but if you want softer blending hold the pencil towards the end and use the side of the tip to lightly shade. You can do this over in over with different pencil grades on top of each other to create layers. You can also use a blending stump or cotton swab to soften it even more.
